official_reference.name: Orchard Sports Injury and Illness Classification System Version 15

multi_type_catalogue.analysis_rule: Preserve semicolon-delimited candidate types and report one informative diagnosis; use the controlled nonspecific primary type so the injury is counted once.

controlled_exceptions.basis: The official diagnosis is Sprain of great toe; both the body area and joint-sprain pathology are explicit even though the workbook's broad IOC Type column is nonspecific.

controlled_exceptions.decision: Neck · Muscle/tendon injury; candidate types muscle_injury;tendinopathy; primary analytical type nonspecific
controlled_exceptions.basis: The official diagnosis explicitly identifies the neck and the two possible tissue families, but it does not establish which family is primary. The candidate types are retained without double-counting the injury.
Soleus trigger points/spasm does not establish a structural muscle injury and the official IOC Type is pain without tissue type specified.

invariants: Existing non-Unknown curated body and injury-type values always win.
An exact-code pathology mapping is accepted only when its body agrees with the existing or uniquely derived body area.
Exact-code and explicit-text pathology disagreement leaves the row unresolved.
Explicit text must yield exactly one controlled body area and exactly one controlled tissue/pathology type.
A reviewed multi-type diagnosis may retain semicolon-delimited candidate types, but contributes once under the controlled nonspecific primary type.
Source values and curated values are never overwritten; effective values and origin are exposed only by the versioned reporting view.
Unknown, nonspecific, broken, unmatched, and conflicting evidence is never upgraded to a named pathology without a separate adjudication.
